title: ForceBody: Force-Paired Parametric Body Motion with Torque Uncertainty
claim: A new dataset attaches ground-truth force and uncertainty labels to a parametric body model, shown on real motion sequences.
layout: 4 panels: two small stacked left, two wide stacked right, colorbars
description: Four panels show the dataset's contents. Panel (a), top left, shows the SKEL biomechanical skeleton next to the SMPL body surface mesh. Panel (b), bottom left, shows one frame twice. The left body is colored by joint torque magnitude, from purple through orange to yellow, with a colorbar on the left. The right body is colored by Monte Carlo uncertainty, in blue-cyan tones, with a colorbar on the right. Green arrows on the feet mark ground reaction forces. Panels (c) and (d) are wide strips on the right. Each overlays many time-lapsed skeletons of a walking sequence on a dark blue background. In (c) the bones are colored by torque on a red-to-yellow scale. In (d) they are colored by uncertainty on a blue-to-cyan scale. Green force arrows appear on the feet in both. The eye goes first to the dense, colorful walking strips.
caption: ForceBody Overview. (a) ForceBody adopts SKEL [15] as the parametric body model: a biomechanical skeleton (left) inside the SMPL surface (right). (b) For one representative frame, the left body is colored by joint torque |τ| (warm), the right by Monte Carlo uncertainty στ (cool). Green arrows on the feet are measured GRF. (c) Force annotations on a walking sequence; bones colored by |τ| (Nm/kg, right colorbar), green arrows on the feet are measured GRF. (d) Uncertainty annotations on the same sequence, bones colored by στ (Nm/kg). The body mesh in (c) and (d) is omitted for visualization clarity.
abstract: Forces and torques drive human motion, central to biomechanics, robotics, and physics-aware animation, yet they are often absent from learning-based motion pipelines for body reconstruction and generation. Some motion datasets provide force annotations, but the paired motion sequences are incompatible with the parametric body models used in modern learning pipelines. In addition, existing datasets typically obtain joint torques through inverse dynamics, which is inherently sensitive to the quality of the input kinematics; however, they do not quantify the reliability of these torque estimates. We close this gap with ForceBody, the first dataset to bring ground truth force supervision into a parametric body representation, shipped with per-sample torque uncertainty. ForceBody pairs the SKEL body model with ground reaction forces and inverse-dynamics joint torques across 10,386 motion trials (9.7M frames, 26.9 hours) from 140 subjects. Each torque label is paired with a per-frame, per-joint uncertainty annotation obtained by Monte Carlo sampling through the inverse dynamics pipeline. We benchmark six architectures (MLP, Conv1D, LSTM, GRU, Mamba2, Transformer) on ground reaction force and joint torque prediction from SKEL motion. As one example use of the released uncertainty, finetuning a Transformer with per-sample uncertainty weighting reduces the MAE of joint torque estimation by 5%. Code and data are at https://github.com/DominoAI-Lab/ForceBody-NeurIPS-ED-2026.
